content:
I am reading our section on Development setup and for now I got confused by at least 3 things. I'm curious to hear what's your opinion and would my suggestions improve the documentation or not?

a) For me it's unclear if headers: Dev setup using elan, VSCode, ccache etc. are alternatives or a conjunction - I need to read a lot into the subsection to understand that VSCode is just a part of the required dev setup and that these steps will not automatically install elan for me.
Suggestion: I think we could use other header weights to make it more obvious? WDYT?

b) You can use [elan](https://github.com/leanprover/elan) to easily switch - wording suggests something completely optional, but when you read more into it, it's like almost a necessary step for efficient development? Maybe it should start with To easily switch, installing elan is strongly suggested?

c) To install elan, you can do so, without installing a default version of Lean,
This is a very confusing sentence. I think it would take at least 10 second less to parse if we removed the bit about default version of Lean? What even is a default version of Lean?
also the bullet about prelude seems like it doesn't belong to that document

I would be happy to review PRs improving the language here, I agree it's not perfect. I would suggest extremely narrow PRs, i.e. each complaint above turning into a separate PR, so reviewing is just a matter or merging a subset and closing the complement, with minimal discussion.
Thanks! I'll work on that and then ping you

Paweł Balawender 🇵🇱 said:

What even is a default version of Lean?

It's the version of Lean you want to run when simply opening a lean file that isn't inside of a project.

Julian Berman said:

Paweł Balawender 🇵🇱 said:

What even is a default version of Lean?

It's the version of Lean you want to run when simply opening a lean file that isn't inside of a project.

[edit]
Okay, but in the context of the sentence that was confusing:

To install elan, you can do so, without installing a default version of Lean,

"Installing a default version of Lean" suggest there is some globally agreed "default" version of Lean. Obviously there will not exist such a version. Above sentence should probably go like "You can install elan independently of any existing or not Lean installation"

I'm not saying the sentence can't be improved in my opinion as well (and Kim explicitly asked for PRs which is what counts). I was making sure you knew what the answer to your question was :)

Paweł Balawender 🇵🇱 said:

"Installing a default version of Lean" suggest there is some globally agreed "default" version of Lean. Obviously there will not exist such a version. Above sentence should probably go like "You can install elan independently of any existing or not Lean installation"

I think you're still slightly misunderstanding the sentence, this is referring to the part you're not quoting, --default-toolchain none otherwise there is such a version. Why that page cares about mentioning that in this context I can't think of a reason, so I probably still agree with your kind of wording change.
